All three compounds are predicted to have a final score of 0.6619, indicating a strong likelihood of interaction with NCI-H2171. The shared target of these compounds at the voltage-dependent T-type calcium channel subunit alpha-1I suggests a common mechanism of action, potentially involving modulation of calcium signaling pathways. The evidence supports a plausible biological pathway where *Eucalyptus gum* compounds may influence NCI-H2171 through this specific target. The consistency in the predicted targets and the high scores across the three paths provide a robust foundation for this relationship, though further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the biological relevance.
